note: Config of the three PILOTS of the PAT-19 protocol v5 instrument (PAT-126, pilots of 2026-10-08): the v5 instrument on ONE task (PR 27), arms A and L complete (local explorer, implementer, corrections, judge, reviewer), under its own protocol name, task-set label and campaign id (the launcher refuses a campaign id without 'pilot' here, and one with 'pilot' under the v5 campaign config). Status: NOT part of the campaign and not a coordinate of the decision; it tunes no value of the decision rule and is not hash-pinned. It carries the instrument keys of the frozen pat-19-campaign-v5.json as they are at the freeze; the pilots 1 and 2 ran under earlier versions of this file (see the campaign_sha256 of their records and the git history), the pilot 3 under the version with isolation.audit_policy. It is the protocol v4 config (pat-19-campaign-v4.json, untouched) with these changes: (1) the instrument repaired by PAT-123 and PAT-124 is switched on for the cloud arms: Claude Code's native Bash sandbox (isolation.cloud_native_sandbox true; the launcher passes --permission-mode dontAsk and --settings; the claude process itself is never wrapped, AGENTS.md R6), audit revision 2 (isolation.audit_revision 2: working-directory-aware audit, a reviewer's flag stays on the review and gives review_unreadable, paths named but absent kept apart, patch capture without caches), the private root per attempt and the hidden-test feedback of v4 kept (20 names, 300 characters per message, 200 per name, 2 corrections); (2) the comparison covers the 12 tasks of the corpus as an explicit ordered list (exploration.comparison_tasks: the six v3 comparison tasks 26, 38, 25, 42, 33, 37 then the six v3 screening tasks 30, 83, 27, 24, 48, 19) recorded under the task-set label exploration.comparison_task_set, distinct from the 'comparison' label of v1 to v4; (3) isolation.allow_read_home lets the cloud shell READ the one file ~/.config/git/ignore (git's default excludes file), so that under the sandbox git no longer prints "unable to access '~/.config/git/ignore': Operation not permitted", whose echo the audit flagged in each reviewer of the trials T2 to T4; the Read tool stays denied on the home; the effect is NOT verified (the pilot is to verify it); (4) Claude Code is pinned to 2.1.285 on every cloud driver (binary_version), checked before the first cloud execution of a launch; (5) isolation.audit_policy journal_under_observed_barrier (added after the pilots 2 and 3, protocol 3.6): host-refused calls do not count, shell findings and tool-result paths under an OS-denied root and the unknown directory are journaled, not contamination; (6) the cap is 16 cloud executions (envelope_recommended; not enforced by the loader). Unchanged: the two arms A (Sonnet alone) and L (Sonnet with the report of the local explorer; no Haiku arm), the fixed candidate qwen3.6-35b-a3b-mlx-4bit without screening, the explorer bounds (60 steps, 900 s) and the reload before each task (one task per launch), the decision rule (L retained iff acceptance(L) >= acceptance(A) and premium per accepted task (L) <= 0.85 x A, compatibility required; absent data is never zero; insufficient evidence keeps the cloud; no promotion), the ground truth (same file and sha256), the dedicated machine. The values of this config were fixed by the coordinator under the maintainer's mandate of 2026-10-08 ('v5, up to the run and the report; the machine is yours all day, you may start and stop what must be'); the maintainer validated nothing value by value. LIMITS: see the protocol v5 (tasks already played downstream in v3 or v4 and already seen by the explorer, non-independent tasks, no Haiku arm, no comparability with v4).

bounds.note: v3, v4 and v5 protocol coordinates (unchanged since v3): explorer_max_seconds 900 (15 min) and explorer_max_steps 60. local_max_seconds and local_max_steps are inherited from v1 and unused (no local implementer); cloud_max_seconds and max_correction_rounds are the v1 operational bounds (the implementer arms and the review). There is no cloud explorer in v5 (no arm E). max_correction_rounds 2 is a protocol coordinate since v4.

isolation.note: Launcher choice, not a protocol coordinate, EXCEPT private_attempt_root, cloud_native_sandbox and audit_revision, which are protocol v5 coordinates pinned by the loader, and allow_read_home, whose only accepted entry is pinned too (see the notes below). LOCAL drivers (sandbox-exec): reads under the user's REAL home are denied by default (deny_home_by_default, true), then only the entries of allow_read_home (relative to the home, empty by default) and the root of the harness executable's environment when it lives in the home are allowed back, plus the bundle and the attempt directory (outside the real home in a normal run); the explicit read-deny list below stays on top as a second layer (the last matching rule wins), together with every checkout/worktree of this repository, the state directory and the parent directory of --envelope/--campaign/--snapshot/--manifest (keep them apart from --work-root). Default-deny is unit-tested on the generated profile and was trial-run on 2026-10-05 with the real omp 18.6.1 and mini-swe-agent 2.4.6 (Qwen3.8-27B MLX 4-bit, allow_read_home empty): both passed, so deny_home_by_default stays true (explicit list exercised with the real local harness by PAT-111 as well). The CLOUD drivers run WITHOUT sandbox-exec (sandbox: false with its reason) and NO read denial applies to them: neither deny_home_by_default nor the cloud list below is enforced for them (kept as data for the audit); an unsandboxed cloud arm can read anything the user can (plugin cache, ~/.config, ~/.ssh, repositories), reach the network, and use the user's implicit credentials (git credential helper through the keychain, gh configuration, ~/.config/foundry), and runs without Foundry hooks (--setting-sources project,local: the R1 guard on gh pr merge / git push does not apply). What stands between a cloud arm and the tracker, secrets and merge is: the best-effort cloud_bash_deny rules, the post-run audit of commands and paths (a record whose tool calls ran a forbidden command or touched the plugin cache, another checkout, the user's configuration, the home or an ancestor of the bundle (the attempt directory and, under private_attempt_root, its private parent are allowed; the work root and above are not) is `contaminated`, undecided, cost kept, never replayed), and the fact that the bundle has no remote. The generated profile is itself denied to a sandboxed arm. Not covered: '(allow default)' leaves Mach access to the security daemon, so denying Library/Keychains does not prevent a keychain query. PROTOCOL v5 (PAT-126): the CLOUD drivers no longer run with bypassPermissions and an open home: under cloud_native_sandbox Claude Code's native Bash sandbox is switched on per execution (see native_sandbox_note); the sentences above about an unsandboxed cloud arm describe v1 to v4 and are kept for the audit's sensitive list, which is unchanged.
isolation.private_attempt_root_note: PAT-121 (kept in v5): each attempt (implementer, correction, review, exploration) is built in <work-root>/private-<attempt>/<attempt>/, so the parent of the attempt directory contains nothing but that attempt: 'ls ..' from the bundle shows no other attempt. The audit is not weakened: the attempt directory and its private parent are allowed, the work root itself and every other attempt under it are listed among the sensitive roots (a read of another attempt is still a contamination), and every other rule (hidden tests, truth file, ~/.config, other checkouts, forbidden commands) is unchanged. Free text of an explorer report rendered into arm L's statement has the resolved spelling of the work root masked (the only one the launcher hands to the arms; another spelling of the same directory, a symlink for instance, is not masked) (explorer bundle path -> bundle-relative path, else <work-root>), so that L is not flagged for reading a path the explorer cited; v1 to v3 rendering unchanged. Each execution (implementer, corrector, reviewer) has its own private root. Set in v4 and v5 (v1 to v3 layout unchanged).
isolation.native_sandbox_note: PAT-124, a protocol v5 coordinate: each cloud execution gets --permission-mode dontAsk (replacing the driver's bypassPermissions) and --settings <json> (native Bash sandbox: reads of the home and of the work root denied to the shell and re-allowed on the attempt directory and on allow_read_home, writes only in the attempt directory and the per-user temp directory, file tools governed by permission rules), GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null and GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 are added to the child's environment, every bundle is built without .claude directories. The HOME, LANG, LC_ALL, LOGNAME, PATH, TMPDIR and USER of the child are untouched (AGENTS.md R6) and the claude process is never wrapped by sandbox-exec. The launcher never observes the operating system enforce the sandbox: the record's audit.barrier says only what it verified, never 'confined'. Accepted limits: the per-user temp directory is shared by all attempts (TMPDIR cannot be changed, R6); dontAsk makes the arms behave otherwise than in v4 (a compound command with a redirection is refused).
isolation.audit_revision_note: PAT-123, a protocol v5 coordinate (accepted only with cloud_native_sandbox): the audit follows the working directory of a command line, imputes a reviewer's flag to the review (the review is then review_unreadable, undecided, never a verdict), records apart a path the arm named that does not exist, and the patch is captured without caches. It over-flags some ordinary gestures (source .venv/bin/activate, break/continue, trap, cd "$(...)", the word cd in a commit message or a heredoc): an accepted cost; the run report reads each flag on the transcript before qualifying it.
isolation.audit_policy_note: PAT-126 (after the pilot 2 of the instrument), a protocol v5 coordinate, accepted only with cloud_native_sandbox and audit_revision 2: where a stream's barrier is settings_transmitted_version_observed the operating system (the native sandbox) is the barrier and the lexical audit a journal. (1) A tool call the host refused as a whole (a permission-mode denial "Permission to use <Tool> has been denied because Claude Code is running in don't ask mode", or a permission-rule denial "denied by your permission settings" / a block of reads outside the working directories) did not run: it contributes nothing to contamination or to the working-directory tracking and is counted per tool in audit.refused_calls. (2) A SHELL finding whose path lies under a root the OS denies to that execution (the sandbox.filesystem.denyRead list the launcher passed, minus its allowRead entries) and the '/<unknown-working-directory>' marker are journaled in audit.journal, not contamination; so is a path shown in a tool RESULT (tool_result:) that lies under such a root, or is a truncated prefix starting with one (text shown in an output is not an access, and the shell that printed it could not read there); every other finding stays decisive (a file-tool path, a path the OS does not deny, a tool-result path outside every denied root, a forbidden command). A reviewer with a decisive finding gives review_unreadable, one with journal-only findings does not. Any other barrier value: strict, as before. ASSUMPTIONS AND LIMITS: it relies on the OS enforcing denyRead for every shell read (observed by the probes P3, P7 and P16 of the trials of 2026-10-08, not for every command); the shared per-user temp directory and other readable places (/Volumes, /private/tmp outside the work root, /Users) are NOT covered by the barrier, so a relative path from an unknown working directory could reach them unseen (limit accepted); deliberate evasion is out of scope.
isolation.allow_read_home_note: PAT-126: the one home file the cloud shell may read. Under the native sandbox every git call printed "unable to access '~/.config/git/ignore': Operation not permitted" (git's default global excludes file, still read when GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null), and the audit flagged the echo as a path of the home in 1 reviewer of each of the trials T2 to T4. In v4 (no sandbox) git read that file. Allowing the READ of that single file (sandbox.filesystem.allowRead) restores what git saw in v4 without opening the home to the shell; the Read/Edit deny rules on the home are unchanged, so the Read TOOL stays denied. The effect is expected, NOT verified (the launcher cannot run claude): the pilot verifies it. Any other entry is refused by the loader. It also feeds the local explorer's profile, where the explicit deny list (.config, last) overrules it: no effect there.

cloud_bash_deny_note: Best-effort Bash permission rules added to --disallowedTools of the two cloud drivers of v4 and v5 (implementer and reviewer) (the loader refuses a real cloud driver whose argv lacks one of them). Claude Code matches a rule against the COMMAND PREFIX: they stop the direct use of the tracker, merge, network and other-agent tools (gh, git push/remote/clone/fetch/pull, curl, wget, claude, codex, omp, ssh, scp, nc, npm, pip install, python -m http, security, open). They are NOT a sandbox: a determined agent evades them (a script, an interpreter one-liner, a renamed binary, an alias, a path-qualified executable, a library call), and the cloud arm keeps the real home, an open network, the user's implicit credentials and bypassPermissions. The post-run audit (command and path audit, contaminated records) detects the direct shapes; it does not prevent anything. Under v5 the native sandbox and dontAsk come on top of these rules (see isolation.native_sandbox_note); they remain best-effort.

dedicated_machine.note: Protocol v2 admission inherited by v3 and v4 (thresholds: maintainer, 2026-10-06; narrowed system patterns: coordinator, 2026-10-07, before any corpus trial; validated by the maintainer on 2026-10-07), applied by the preflight of compare-exploration when arm L runs (screen-exploration is refused in v4; in v2 and v3 it applied before every screening task): refuse when a process outside the allow-list below holds more than max_other_process_rss_gib of resident memory (ps -axo rss=,command=), or when the free memory percentage of memory_pressure is under min_free_percent (35: replaces the 'swap de départ' threshold of the ticket's original AC; swap in use does not come down without a reboot, and the process rule is the real guard, see pat-19-preflight-v2-2026-10-06.json#dedicated_machine_measurement). Both commands are already in the launcher's read-only list. An unreadable output refuses. Only a process NAME (application name or executable basename, never an argument) is recorded with the observed values. The system patterns are deliberately narrow: /System/Library/ (daemons and frameworks), /usr/libexec|sbin|bin, /sbin, /Library/Apple and kernel_task; NOT /System/Applications/ (consumer apps such as Mail or Photos) nor /System/Volumes/Preboot/Cryptexes/App/ (Safari/WebKit), which are ordinary memory consumers.

exploration.note: Report format of the explorers: one JSON object {"files": [repo-relative paths], "functions": [{"file", "name"}], "rationale": str}; all three keys required. Read from <scratch>/report.json when the arm wrote one, else from the final message of its stream. A missing or unusable report, an exploration cut by a bound (time or steps) or a bundle whose git status changed is a refusal (score 0), never a void attempt. Only the FIRST 10 functions of a report count for function recall and are passed to the implementer of arm L (report_render_limits.max_functions must stay 10).

ground_truth.note: the single source of the ground truth: the launcher loads this committed file and refuses (campaign load, code 2, before any attempt) a file whose sha256 differs

protocol_coordinates.note: These determine the score or the verdicts of the comparison and are stated in the protocol (the protocol v5 and the inherited sections of v4, v3 and v2): they ARE protocol coordinates; once the v5 is frozen, changing one opens a protocol v6.

function_cap.rationale: only the first 10 functions of a report count for function recall and reach the implementer of arm L (report_render_limits.max_functions must equal it)

protocol_coordinates.function_name_match: a reported function name matches a true function in the same file when it equals the qualified name or its last component
protocol_coordinates.empty_report_precision: a valid report with no file has file precision 0 (undefined ratio counted as 0, so the precision floor cannot be met by saying nothing)
protocol_coordinates.localization_ground_truth: recall uses the product files and functions only (the judge's own classification: SOURCE_PREFIXES, not tests, not documentation); precision counts a reported file as correct when the merged diff really changed or created it, product or not; files the diff adds are not counted in recall and functions that do not exist at the base SHA are not counted in function recall: an explorer cannot find what does not exist yet. A removed line is read in the base source, an added line in the merged source; the diff algorithm is pinned (myers)
protocol_coordinates.premium_work_definition: premium work = unweighted sum of the four billing token classes (input, cached input, cache write, output) over ALL models, explorer included: a Haiku explorer counts as premium, local tokens do not; a limit: an economy model's token weighs the same as a premium one, hence the per-model breakdown in the report
protocol_coordinates.refused_report_in_comparison: when an explorer of the comparison yields no usable report, its implementer runs on the plain statement and the explorer's cost stays counted (the end-to-end cost of using the explorer); a contaminated or twice-cut explorer leaves the arm undecided for that task
protocol_coordinates.quality_bounds_on_undecided: quality compares acceptance counts with undecided tasks as bounds: pass only if it holds in the worst case, fail only if it fails in the best case, else unavailable
protocol_coordinates.economy_unavailable_cases: premium per accepted task is unavailable (never zero) when a compared task is undecided, spent work is unknown, a premium total is unknown or an arm accepted no task

exploration.one_task_per_launch_note: Protocol v3 reload rule, inherited by v4 and v5 (written in advance): the launcher loads no model, so with this flag screen-exploration (refused in v4) plays at most ONE not-yet-decided task of the candidate per launch and compare-exploration at most ONE comparison task (all its requested arms) per launch, then exits 0 and prints 'pat19-v3: work_remains=yes' or 'pat19-v3: work_remains=no' on stdout. The operator unloads and reloads the pinned model between launches (pat-19-v3-operator.md). Resume semantics are unchanged (a decided task is skipped). The per-task reload is attested by the operator script plus one session (one ledger preflight) per task, not by the launcher. Same rule in v4 and v5 (the line printed is unchanged: pat19-v3: work_remains=...).
exploration.v5_note: PAT-126: the comparison runs on an explicit ordered list of corpus PRs (the pilot plays PR 27 only), recorded under the task-set label 'pat-19-v5-pilot' (not 'comparison', the label of v1 to v4). Every listed PR must be in the corpus manifest and the snapshot. Every one of the 12 tasks was already played downstream before (the six v3 comparison tasks in the v3 comparison pat-19-x3compare-1, the six v3 screening tasks in the v4 comparison pat-19-x4compare-1) and already seen by the local explorer: they are not fresh, and they are not independent (see the protocol limits). The candidate is fixed by the protocol (no screening results are needed; screen-exploration is refused). The ground truth file covers these tasks (same file and sha256 as v2 to v4).

min_free_disk_gib.rationale: launcher safety margin for model files and bundles; the protocol states no disk threshold

swap_metric.rationale: extra swap is measured as the maximum, over local attempts, of (swap after - swap before); the protocol does not define how to measure it

explorer_tool_names.rationale: the read-only tool set of the local explorer is --tools=read,grep,glob. The maintainer validated the read-only intent on 2026-10-06 as read,grep,find,ls; the toy trial of omp 18.6.1 refused it ("Unknown tool in --tools: ls"; find is "unavailable in this session"; the built-ins include read, grep, glob), so the names were corrected to the same trio as the cloud explorer (Read/Grep/Glob) before the freeze. The loader accepts only read, grep, glob.

report_source_and_prompt.rationale: the pinned tool sets have no file-writing tool, so the prompt asks for the JSON as the final message and the launcher reads it from the stream; an arm-written <scratch>/report.json is also accepted. The shapes of the final messages were pinned by the real toy trials of 2026-10-06 and, with the frozen prompt, of 2026-10-07 (pat-19-preflight-v2-2026-10-06.json: drivers, final_prompt_trial)

report_render_limits.rationale: a report appended to a statement is cut at 20 files and 1500 rationale characters, with a visible note; the scoring is not affected. The cap of 10 functions is a protocol coordinate (exploration.protocol_coordinates.function_cap)

envelope_recommendation.rationale: the caps below are a recommendation for the operator's envelope file (the launcher never writes one); the envelope stays the operator's

explorer_bundle_unchanged_check.rationale: the launcher records git status --porcelain of the bundle before and after each exploration (local and cloud); a modified or unreadable bundle refuses the exploration (score 0, never replayed). Kept in v4 for the local explorer (no cloud explorer is declared); in v2/v3 it was needed because the cloud explorer is not sandboxed (Bash open): read-only behaviour is observed, not enforced

statement_footer:
---
Launcher note (identical for every arm): work only inside this repository. Do not create virtual environments, install packages or create node_modules in the tree; use the interpreter already on PATH. Do not create or edit test configuration files (conftest.py, pytest.ini, pyproject.toml, tox.ini, setup.cfg, sitecustomize.py, *.pth).

prompts.implement: Implement the task described in {statement_file}. Work only inside the current repository: change the product code and add tests if useful. Run the relevant tests, then stop when you consider the task done.
prompts.correct: The task is described in {statement_file}. A previous attempt is already applied in this repository. Apply the corrections listed in {feedback_file}, run the relevant tests, then stop.
prompts.review: Independently review the uncommitted change in this repository (git diff HEAD) against the task in {statement_file}. Do not modify any file. Write {review_file} as JSON: {"verdict": "PASS" or "BLOCK", "findings": ["..."]}.
prompts.explore: Prepare the task described in {statement_file} by exploring this repository READ-ONLY: do not modify any file, do not run tests, do not write anything. You have at most {max_duration} (and at most {max_steps} tool steps where the harness counts them): answer with the JSON BEFORE reaching them, an exploration cut by a bound is refused and scores 0. Find where the change must be made. Your final message must be exactly one JSON object and nothing else: {"files": ["repo-relative path", ...], "functions": [{"file": "repo-relative path", "name": "function or Class.method"}], "rationale": "short explanation"}. List the files and the functions that need to change, not the ones you merely read; at most 10 functions, most relevant first (only the first 10 count).

exploration_screening.note: Not played in v5 (the candidate is fixed, exploration.fixed_candidate; screen-exploration is refused). Kept so that the v2 schema is satisfied and the rule stays readable. MAIN metric = mean FUNCTION recall over the 6 tasks (maintainer decision 2026-10-06, before the freeze: each task's truth is a single product file and 5 of the 6 screening tasks share linear.py, so file recall is near-trivial). Candidates were the two frozen ones of v3 (in v4 the candidates list holds only qwen3.6-35b-a3b-mlx-4bit, fixed) and the v3 screening was complete only when both had their 6 tasks decided. Eligible = mean file precision >= 0.5; the best mean function recall is compared to retained_function_recall_min BEFORE any tie (below 0.5: STOP 'conserver le cloud', also for a tie; exactly 0.5 is retained); then a tie goes to the shortest total duration, and a tie still unresolved to the candidate listed first in candidates. STOP also when no candidate has mean file precision >= 0.5. File recall is measured and reported but does not decide. A task whose truth has no function (none today) is excluded from the function-recall mean. A refused or contaminated attempt counts 0 on every metric and never blocks the screening: an assumed departure from 'absent data is never zero', limited to this filter (the comparison keeps unknown as unknown). Inherited from v2 and v3; kept readable, not applied in v5.

exploration_comparison.note: arm L is retained only if compatibility AND quality AND economy all pass on the 1 task: its acceptance rate >= A's AND its premium tokens per accepted task (explorer included; local tokens do not count) <= 0.85 x A's, and compatibility (the v1 machine criterion: no external signal, extra swap under extra_swap_gib_max) passes. v5 has no arm E. A task whose arm record is undecided (contaminated, review_unreadable, tool error, cap) is undecided, not failed; quality compares acceptance counts with undecided tasks as bounds. Rule unchanged from v2, v3 and v4; the pilot decides nothing.

compare_exploration.justification: One task, 2 arms, per arm at most 1 implementer + 2 corrections and 3 reviews = 6 executions: 2 x 6 = 12 <= 16 (the cap holds the worst case and leaves room for one replay of a round cut before its verdict). premium_tokens 8 000 000 is 500 000 per execution of 16, the per-execution allowance of v3 and v4. wall_clock 30 000 s covers 12 cloud executions at ~10 min plus 2 x 900 s of local exploration with margin.

local_explorer.note: Protocol v2 read-only local explorer: omp 18.6.1 as the v1 local_harness plus --tools=read,grep,glob (no edit, write or bash tool), the bundle READ-ONLY in the sandbox profile (only the attempt scratch writable), bounded by explorer_max_seconds/steps. Trial-run on 2026-10-06 (see evidence): with Qwen3.6-35B-A3B MLX 4-bit, sandbox on, bundle read-only, deny-home: exit 0, 14.0 s, 4 steps, bundle unchanged, final-message report parsed. The first argv (--tools=read,grep,find,ls) was refused by omp.

session_log.layout_note: Verified on 2026-10-05 (PAT-111): the launcher's reading of <projects_dir>/*/<session>.jsonl equals the host's own result.usage exactly for the cloud drivers (three in v3; implementer and reviewer in v4), one file per session id. Conditional on the launcher's assertion, from the stream's system/init event, that the arm's tools are a subset of allowed_tools (Bash, Edit, Read, Write; so no sub-agent, workflow, web or scheduling tool): a record whose init event lists any other tool, or has none, is refused (tool_error).

cloud_implementer_current.note: Claude Code 2.1.285 headless, current routed implementer profile (Sonnet 5.5, effort medium). The first 2026-10-05 trial ran with `--disallowedTools Agent` only; the FINAL argv (29 tool names + the cloud_bash_deny rules) was then trial-run on the toy task on 2026-10-05 (init: exactly Bash, Edit, Read, Write) and passed, see the evidence. Bare Claude Code with the protocol's model and effort: no Foundry plugin, hook, agent definition (not the Eiffel or Maigret definitions), --permission-mode bypassPermissions, tools restricted to Read/Edit/Write/Bash with Bash otherwise unrestricted except for the best-effort deny rules. PAT-126 (protocol v5): the launcher replaces --permission-mode bypassPermissions by dontAsk and appends --settings (isolation.cloud_native_sandbox); the argv above is the v4 one, kept so that the pinned tool set and deny rules are unchanged. Claude Code is pinned to 2.1.285 by binary_version (output format '<version> (Claude Code)'), checked before the first cloud execution of a launch; the trials T2 to T4 of 2026-10-08 observed only this version.

The arm runs unsandboxed with the AGENTS.md R6 environment intact (real HOME, LANG, LC_ALL, LOGNAME, PATH, TMPDIR, USER) in the disposable bundle; its tool calls are audited after the run. Consequences, not mitigated by the launcher: real home, open network, the user's implicit credentials, no Foundry hook (no R1 guard); see cloud_bash_deny and isolation.note.

qwen3.6-35b-a3b-mlx-4bit.generation_parameters: server and harness defaults, not overridden by the launcher (no temperature, top_p, top_k, seed or max_tokens is passed)

candidates_note: model = the LM Studio model key, which is also the identifier the operator gives at load (lms load <key> -c 65536 --identifier <key> --parallel 1) and the name the harness sends; the HF repo of the protocol is kept as hf_repo_provenance. The operator loads, the launcher loads nothing. The preflight reads the loaded instance (lms ps --json) and refuses when its model key differs, its quantization differs or its context length is below min_context (65536, a frozen coordinate: LM Studio ignored -c for some MLX builds). File digests, chat-template digest and generation parameters are recorded here and in pat-19-preflight-2026-10-05.json; they are not recomputed by the launcher. Generation parameters are the server and harness defaults, not overridden. Protocols v4 and v5 keep only qwen3.6-35b-a3b-mlx-4bit, unchanged (qwen3-coder is not compared: no new screening).

correction_feedback.note: PAT-121, kept unchanged in v5 (PAT-126) (values fixed by the coordinator, confirmed by the maintainer on 2026-10-07 before any trial: max_failures 20, max_message_chars 300, max_name_chars 200, and the 2 correction rounds of bounds). After a judge REFUSED verdict the corrector's feedback file adds the failing or erroring hidden tests (junit classname::name cut to max_name_chars, a parametrized id can carry test data), at most max_failures of them, each with the junit failure message cut to max_message_chars characters (whitespace collapsed, the candidate's location replaced by <bundle>, the judge's temporary directory by <tmp>), and the line 'N shown of M' (the count not shown is M - N). Never the test source code (the test module and name are visible, and a message can carry a path under the bundle; only the bundle path and the judge's temporary directory are masked); but the pytest message can carry the expression of an assertion and the expected values, so a corrector can fit code to the tests (the same for both arms). A collection error only yields a collection-failure message: the feedback then teaches nothing (its share in v3 is unknown). A refusal with no test list (timeout, harness files changed, candidate fault) adds nothing. Identical for arms A and L (same code path). Absent from the v1, v2 and v3 configs, where the key is refused at load: their feedback is unchanged. Accepted under protocols v4 and after. Each correction record carries counters only (feedback: failing_shown, failing_total, collection_failure), never text.
